title: Beyond the Bellman Recursion: A Pontryagin-Guided Framework for Non-Exponential Discounting
claim: A familiar special case sits at the intersection of two properties; violating either one breaks the standard solution method.
layout: 1 panel, Venn diagram of two overlapping circles in a rounded box, labels inside regions
description: A single Venn diagram inside a rounded light-green box. A blue circle on the left is labeled 'Multiplicative' above it. An orange circle on the right is labeled 'Time-Homogeneous'. The blue-only region reads 'Case 1: Bellman OK, non-stationary'. The orange-only region reads 'Case 2: time-inconsistent equilibrium'. The grey lens where the circles overlap holds 'Exponential' in bold red, which is where the eye goes first. The green area outside both circles is labeled at the bottom 'Case 3: general D(s,t)'. Colors separate the regions. Text is bold serif and there are no arrows or icons. The figure shows how the discount kernels divide into cases.
caption: Discount-kernel taxonomy. Exponential discounting lies at the intersection of multiplicativity [ref] and time homogeneity [ref]. Violating either property invalidates recursion-based methods.
abstract: Most value-based and actor--critic reinforcement learning methods rely on Bellman-style recursions, yet these recursions collapse under non-exponential discounting common in human preferences and survival processes. We show the breakdown is structural: exponential discounting sits at a fragile intersection of multiplicativity and time homogeneity, and violating either property breaks standard dynamic programming. To overcome this, we propose Pontryagin-Guided Direct Policy Optimization (PG-DPO), a variational framework that abandons recursion and couples the Pontryagin Maximum Principle with Monte Carlo rollouts via an Adjoint-MC projection enforcing pointwise Hamiltonian maximization. Across multi-dimensional hyperbolic and survival-discount benchmarks, PG-DPO improves accuracy and stability where equation-driven solvers and critic-based baselines diverge.
